THE FIRST REVIEW OF 1.24.31 (MAKE STATION -- AI_STATION; the usual four floats added to a floatless duplex in
AI_CONTROL's takeTurns; the block grammars -- AI_ACTIONS' grammarFor, sent by Chat and the bench's solve, AI.callServer).
Reviewed at d141e58 (wip 1.24.31) by a reviewer that did not write the rules. 1.24.30 as it was (ad0d654) is loaded beside
it for every comparison (lib.js OLD(), from git show).

HOW TO REPLAY
  node tests/fixtures/station_review1_1231/replay.js [id-prefix]     (jsdom; about 4 s)
  node tests/fixtures/station_review1_1231/make_grammar.js            (E-G: runs the grammar samples through llama.cpp's
                                                                       parser, tools/gbnf_check.py, and rewrites
                                                                       grammar_results.json; needs LLAMA_LIB, LLAMA_VOCAB)
  replay.js runs E-G live when LLAMA_LIB and LLAMA_VOCAB exist (b11435's libllama.so, ggml-vocab-qwen2.gguf), else from
  grammar_results.json (and says so when the grammars have changed since). load.js and sim.js are copies of the third
  1.24.30 review's harness, read before use; lib.js and every case are this review's own.

COUNTS
  303 cases: 212 AGREE, 91 DISAGREE (13 high, 42 medium, 36 low), in about 22 root causes
    A  MAKE STATION blocks       114 cases, 31 DISAGREE (7 high, 10 medium, 14 low)
    B  routing                    74 cases, 26 DISAGREE (4 high, 17 medium, 5 low)
    C  read as a station          25 cases,  8 DISAGREE (2 high, 5 medium, 1 low)
    D  the floatless duplex       28 cases,  6 DISAGREE (4 medium, 2 low)
    E  grammars (G: parser)       47 cases, 19 DISAGREE (5 medium, 14 low)
       grammars (P: when sent)    15 cases,  1 DISAGREE (1 medium)
  tests/station.js passes (46) on the same tree.

FINDINGS (highest harm first)

1. [high] Anything MADE about a station is routed as the station, and loses its own tool. B-52 B-53 B-54 B-56 (high),
   B-55 B-57 B-58 B-59 B-60 B-61 B-62 B-73 (medium), B-63..B-66 (low).
   Lantern did: "Make a slide deck about lift stations for a city council meeting", "Make a spreadsheet of lift station
   pump run hours", "Make flashcards about lift station parts", "Plan a maintenance schedule for our lift station", a
   budget, a checklist, a calendar, a table, a map, a cartoon, a bar chart, a quiz, a logo, a timeline, a lesson plan:
   each is offered MAKE STATION alone (1.24.30 offered slides, sheet, cards, plan, doc, drawing). asks() returns true for
   any "make/create/draw/plan/design ... lift|pump|sewage ... station" with no drawing named (WHOLE), and relevant() then
   drops every tool that is not whole. B-73: "... control circuit and piping, then make a slide deck about it" is not
   split, and the deck is never asked for.
   Right (rule 7): a question is the station whole only when the thing to make IS the station (its drawings, its parts
   list, its sequence, its checks); when the question names another tool's thing (slides, sheet, table, chart, cards,
   plan, schedule, calendar, document, checklist, map, picture, quiz, logo) that tool stays, and a whole station beside
   it is one part of a split question.

2. [high] A loose word in the question overrules the block's count of pumps. A-97, A-98 (high), A-99 (medium).
   Lantern did: "Design a duplex lift station where one pump runs and the other stands by" -> one pump ("1 pumps: the
   question asks for 1 (the block said 2)"); "Upgrade a simplex lift station to a duplex" -> one pump; "Design a triplex
   lift station ... two pumps run at peak flow" -> two. pumpsAsked() (AI_PUMP_STATION) tests simplex / one pump first,
   then duplex / two pumps, then triplex; AI_STATION's spec() overrules the block with it and says the question asked.
   Right: overrule the block only on a count the question gives unambiguously (one count, nothing contradicting it:
   "duplex" with "one pump runs" is a duplex); else keep the block's count, or say both.

3. [high] Any later number on the pumps line becomes the count. A-90, A-91, A-93 (high), A-94 (medium), A-92 (low).
   Lantern did: "pumps 2 x 5 HP" and "pumps 2 rated 200 gpm at 50 ft" -> count 5 / 200 -> sent back "keep it to 4 pumps
   or fewer, like: pumps 4" (a line to copy that turns a duplex into a quadplex with no control circuit); "pumps 2 (1
   duty, 1 standby)" and "pumps: 1 duty + 1 standby" -> one pump (a simplex); "pumps 2, 10 hp each" for Adam's question ->
   "2 pumps: the question asks for 2 (the block said 10)". parse(): if (!pr.count || pr.count < +x || !pr.ids.length)
   pr.count = +x -- with no tags, every bare number overwrites the count.
   Right: the first number after "pumps" (or a count word) is the count; a number followed by hp, kW, gpm, L/s, ft, m,
   or inside brackets after the count, is not; "1 duty + 1 standby" is two.

4. [high] One pump with a lag float: a control circuit that does not do what Lantern says it does. A-105.
   Lantern did: "pumps 1 / floats off lead lag alarm" (a duplex's floats on a simplex question): blocks() writes FS3
   "lag on" into a one-pump MAKE CONTROL with no alternator; AI_CONTROL puts FS1, FS2 and FS3 in series in M1's rung
   with no holding contact (the pump runs only while the water is above the lag float, and short-cycles there); drawn
   with no problem; the sequence and the checks say "As the water rises to FS2 (pump on), the pump starts; it pumps the
   well down to FS1 (off) and stops."
   Right: for one pump a lag float is dropped and said (or the block questioned); the control Lantern writes itself must
   be the one its own sequence describes (rule 2).

5. [high] Heights written before their floats are shifted one float up, and the shifted line is handed back to copy.
   A-37.
   Lantern did: "floats 2 ft off, 3 ft lead, 4 ft lag, 5 ft alarm" -> off 3 ft, lead 4 ft, lag 5 ft, alarm none; the
   levels refuse it ("give every float its height, or none") with the line "like float FS1 \"off\" 3 ft, float FS2
   \"lead on\" 4 ft, float FS3 \"lag on\" 5 ft, float FS4 \"high level alarm\"" -- each height wrong. floatList() gives
   each job the text after it.
   Right: a height before the first job word goes with it (the order of number and word is the same throughout the
   line); or the block questioned without a wrong line to copy (rule 3, rule 7).

6. [high] Read as a station, the drawings disagree about the floats. C-11, C-12 (high); A-111 (low, the same in a MAKE
   STATION block, where it is at least said as "not read").
   Lantern did: a station question answered with MAKE CONTROL whose floats are written "level LS1 ..." or "fs FS1 ..."
   (words MAKE CONTROL reads as floats): the control is drawn with LS1-LS3 (or FS1-FS2); AI_STATION's lenient parse does
   not read those words, so the float levels and the parts list show the usual four floats FS1-FS4 (said as "the usual
   floats"), two of which, or all of which, are in no circuit.
   Right: the station reads every float word MAKE CONTROL reads (SROLES' floats lacks "level", "fs", "ls"), so one
   station has one set of floats.

7. [medium] "duplex" or "pump station" alone makes a question a lift station. B-43..B-51.
   Lantern did: the plumbing and wiring of a two-family "duplex", a duplex receptacle's wiring and parts list, a duplex
   air compressor (two questions), cooling tower and chilled-water pumps, a booster, an irrigation and a water
   distribution pump station: each is MAKE STATION alone (a wet well, floats, an alternating relay, a force main), and
   the code or schematic tool is dropped. 1.24.30 already offered a wet well's MAKE PIPING to most of these (the
   STATION word list of AI_PUMP_STATION); now the whole lift station comes with it.
   Right (rule 7): a station question names a wet well, sewage, wastewater, a lift station, a sump or storm water;
   "duplex" with none of these, and booster / irrigation / distribution / chilled / cooling tower / compressor / receptacle
   / apartment, are not one.

8. [medium] The floatless duplex rule adds a wet well's floats to any two motors on an alternator. D-18 D-19 D-20 D-21
   (medium), D-22 D-23 (low).
   Lantern did: two air compressors, two booster pumps, two chilled-water pumps, two fans on a timer, a compressor whose
   pressure switch is written 'switch PS1 "pressure switch"', two vacuum pumps -- with no float written, each gets
   "the floats FS1 (off), FS2 (lead on), FS3 (lag on) and FS4 (high level alarm)" and is drawn as a lift station. (1.24.30
   sent them back asking for floats -- also not right, but it drew nothing.) The rule looks at no label and no question.
   Right: add the four only when the circuit or the question is a wet well's (pumps of a lift station, sump, sewage);
   otherwise question it as the pressure-switch case is questioned (no float line).

9. [medium] Read as a station, a contradiction between the blocks is not said. C-13, C-14.
   Lantern did: a one-pump MAKE CONTROL for Adam's two-pump question -> the control of one pump beside a piping of two,
   the sequence "Each time the pumps stop, the alternating relay changes over" (there is none), and "2 pumps: the
   question asks for 2 (the block said 1)" as if the control were made for two. A control of three floats (no lag) with
   a levels block of four (with a lag): both drawn as written, listed as one station, the sequence promising the lag
   float runs both pumps; nothing said.
   Right: what the given blocks disagree on is said (or the station questioned once, naming it).

10. [medium] A station question answered with a block that is not a station's drawing: that block alone, nothing more.
    C-21, C-22, C-25.
    Lantern did: MAKE SCHEMATIC holding the piping's lines (read as MAKE PIPING by AI_PUMP_STATION, which AI_STATION's
    viewOf passes by): the piping drawn, the turn ended, the control and levels neither made nor said missing; on the
    bench "made a schematic, not station" with nothing asked. MAKE DRAWING (a grid picture): shown, the turn ended.
    1.24.30 (AI_PARTS) asked for each part still missing; a whole question is not split now, so nothing does.
    Right: a station question's block read as piping is read as the station (its piping as written); any other block
    gets the station asked for once.

11. [medium] A float the block wrote is dropped without a word. A-109, A-110.
    Lantern did: "floats off lead lag alarm" + 'float FS5 "high high level alarm"' -> four floats, FS5 taking the alarm's
    place and its label "high level alarm" (the floats line's bare "alarm" merges with any alarm); a 5-float design with
    'float FS2 "lag off"' -> FS2 merged into the off float and gone.
    Right: two alarms with different labels kept (MAKE CONTROL draws both); a lag pump's own off float kept (MAKE CONTROL
    has lagOff) or said.

12. [medium] The guide's own float line, copied, is not "the usual". A-88.
    Lantern did: 'float FS2 "lead on" <height>' copied (with "pumps 2", no floats line) -> a duplex of two floats (off
    added; no lag, no alarm).
    Right (the module's own header): the guide's lines copied as they stand read as the usual -- four floats.

13. [medium] The block grammars hold out lines Lantern reads. E-G07 E-G08 E-G09 E-G11 E-G12 (medium); E-G10, E-G13..E-G18,
    E-G30..E-G32, E-G37, E-G38, E-G42, E-G43 (low).
    llama.cpp b11435's parser (Qwen2 vocabulary) holds out: STATION "Wet well: 10 ft deep", "force main 4 in", "control
    voltage 120 V AC", "voltage: 230 V", "Number of pumps: 2", "- pumps 2", "gate valves", "alarm horn", "Type: duplex",
    "PUMPS 2", a blank line, "sump 6 ft"; CONTROL "e-stop PB0", "run light LT1 M1", "time delay relay TR1"; PIPING "flap
    check valve", "eccentric plug valve"; LEVELS "FS1: off float at 2 ft", "1. float FS1 ...". Lantern's parsers read
    every one as meant. grammarWords is a hand list narrower than SROLES / LEADS (and PROLE, LROLE, ROLE, tidy1), with no
    bullet, number, all-capitals or blank line. Held on a correction or after prose, the model is pushed off the line it
    would write -- onto another allowed word ("Note", "valves", "well") with the rest of its line.
    Right: the words from the same tables the parser reads (every role word and every LEADS first word), case-blind, an
    optional bullet or number, and blank lines.

14. [medium] A correction that names another kind is held to the old kind's grammar. E-P13.
    Lantern did: MAKE HYDRAULIC with a compressor for a pneumatic question -> "a compressor is pneumatic ... for
    compressed air write MAKE PNEUMATIC", and the next call is held to root ::= "MAKE HYDRAULIC: ". (The same for
    PNEUMATIC's "write MAKE HYDRAULIC for an oil circuit".) Before the grammar, the model could do as told.
    Right: no grammar, or the named kind's, when a problem tells the model to write another MAKE kind.

15. [medium] Inch marks in a floats line lose the heights. A-42.
    Lantern did: 'floats off 24", lead 36", lag 48", alarm 60"' -> the " marks read as quotes, every height dropped,
    nothing said; the levels then say "Not to scale: give each float its height".
    Right: 24" is 24 in (as the float lines read 2'6"), or the line questioned.

16. [medium] A four-letter ISA tag is renamed in the levels drawing. A-51.
    Lantern did: 'float LSHH1 "high level alarm" 5 ft' -> the control and the parts list say LSHH1, the levels drawing FS1
    (MAKE LEVELS takes tags of 1-3 letters).
    Right: one tag for one float in every drawing.

17. [medium] A pipe's size read as the inlet's invert. A-63.
    Lantern did: "inlet 8 in" -> the inlet invert at 8 in above the floor, and the levels' steps say the inlet's invert
    is "above them" (the floats).
    Right: "8 in" after "inlet" with nothing else is a size (as heightOf passes over "8 in gravity sewer"); no invert.

18. [medium] More pumps than Lantern draws are sent back with a line that changes the station. A-100.
    Lantern did: "Design a lift station with five pumps", "pumps 5" -> "keep it to 4 pumps or fewer, like: pumps 4".
    Right: say what it cannot draw (the control, as for three and four) and draw the rest, or decline; never a line that
    makes another station than the one asked for.

19. [medium] A sump's "low level" and "high level" floats. A-106.
    Lantern did: "pumps 1 / floats low level, high level" -> "low level" not read, "high level" made the alarm, an off and
    a lead float added: three floats for the block's two.
    Right: as MAKE CONTROL reads them (second 1.24.30 review): low level stops, high level starts.

20. [low] What the parts list and the checks say beyond the drawings. A-85, A-101, A-102.
    The pumps P1, P2 are not in the parts list when the piping is not drawn (control and levels asked); a triplex or
    quadplex's checks say "Lift FS3 (lag on) with FS2 up: both pumps run" and "the alarm light comes on" with no control
    circuit drawn.

21. [low] Wording, and silent drops or choices. A-59 ("Wet well, 10 ft below grade deep"), A-60 ("8 ft diameter 12 ft
    deep": no depth, nothing said -- heightOf takes "12 ft" as the diameter's), A-62 (inlet "8 in gravity sewer at"),
    A-64 (inlet labelled "invert"), A-72 ("valves gate, plug or ball" -> gate, not said), A-73 ("check valves: swing"
    dropped), A-82 (a note line parsed and then used nowhere: not drawn, not in the document, not said), A-92 (see 3),
    "1 pumps" (in A-97's said).

22. [low] Defaults and scope. A-107 (two pumps "taking turns, the usual lift station" for "a sump pump"), A-108 (a block
    titled "Simplex sump station" drawn as two pumps), C-19 (MAKE STATION for a question about the control circuit alone
    draws all three drawings: spec() takes all three when fewer than two are asked), B-20 ("Write the commissioning
    checklist for a duplex lift station" is not the station: asks() names commissioning but needs a drawing verb).

WHAT HELD (selected AGREEs)
  - The guide's example and 60-odd right variants (counts as words, colons, equals, bullets, numbers, capitals, slashes,
    other names for the jobs, "float switches:", tags, a line per pump; heights in ft, m, mm, in, ft and in, primes,
    decimal commas, mixed units, elevations, below grade; floats top down, tags numbered from the top; set B's form;
    a low level alarm; well, inlet, main, plug/gate/ball valves, supply as quoted, bare, "control voltage", "voltage:";
    horn; no lights): each drawn whole and right -- the ladder simulated (the lead float starts one pump, held in to the
    off float, the pumps take turns, the lag runs both and holds to the off float, the alarm light only at the alarm
    float, an overload drops only its pump), each pump's check then shutoff valve, the levels the same floats in order
    and to scale (measured), the parts list naming every rung, valve and float and nothing else, the sequence and the
    checks naming the floats drawn, every default said (A-01..A-58 bar the above).
  - Placeholders read as nothing (A-87); prose and typos said as not read (A-31, A-32); floats out of order, two heights
    for one float, floats above the well's depth questioned with the line (A-54..A-56); a float with no job questioned
    with its line (A-112); a simplex right (A-103, A-104).
  - Read as a station: the 35B's two control blocks, the 2B's floatless duplex, set B's control, piping alone, levels
    alone, control and levels, all three, MAKE SCHEMATIC with the control's lines (C-01..C-10); the same blocks for a
    question about one drawing stay that drawing (C-15..C-18); Chat one call (C-20); the bench passes the 1.24.30 blocks
    and the 2B's floatless control (C-23, C-24, D-28).
  - The floatless duplex: four floats added, said and wired right, with lights, supply, a horn on FS4, a light on the
    alternator, the 35B's "alternating"/"starter" words (D-01..D-08); every circuit with floats, with "level" floats,
    with a start button, three pumps, a pressure or temperature switch, and plain starters is as 1.24.30 drew it or
    questioned it (D-09..D-17, D-24..D-27).
  - Routing: every one of the 298 other bench questions is offered the same tools, split the same and given the same
    short prompt as on 1.24.30; their whole instructions differ only by "a pump station (Writer, and each drawing in
    Draw), " in the list (B-71, B-72). Single drawings, PLC and Arduino programs, fire pumps, a house's sump, boilers,
    septic tanks, drinking-water wells, hydraulics stay off the station (B-21..B-42); a station and its PLC program is
    now split into the station and the program (B-74, better than 1.24.30).
  - Grammars: each parses in llama.cpp b11435; prose before, inside and after a block, fences, a refusal, another kind's
    block and a missing title are held out (E-G19..E-G25, E-G33, E-G34, E-G39, E-G44, E-G47). Sent on the block asked for
    after prose, on corrections and on the next part only; never on a question's first call, a later conversation turn's
    first call, a sum, or to a server without /props; a server that refuses one gets the request again without it and
    no grammar after; a context-size refusal does not turn grammars off; the old-form SCHEMATIC correction still lets
    the right answer through (E-P01..E-P12, E-P14, E-P15).

NOT RUN OR NOT CHECKED
  - No model at all: every reply is scripted (no 35B, no 4B/2B/0.8B run, no bench workflow). Nothing here says how a
    model writes under a grammar; whether a held-out line pushes a model onto a worse one (finding 13) is reasoned, not
    measured.
  - The grammars were run through llama.cpp's parser with Qwen2's vocabulary file only (tools/gbnf_check.py), not with
    the Qwen3.5 models' own vocabulary, and not sent to a running llama-server (whether it takes "grammar" beside
    chat_template_kwargs in /v1/chat/completions was not tried).
  - No real browser: the station's view, its Draw buttons, Writer and the PDF were not opened, and no drawing was looked
    at (how a drawing looks is Adam's to judge). The levels' scale was measured from the shapes, not seen.
  - The in-page (device) engine ignores opts.grammar: read in the code (D.complete), not run.
  - A custom endpoint beside a detected llama-server (AI.endpoint() !== AI.server.endpoint) was not tried.
  - The standards the document cites (Ten States 42.52, 44.4, 42.64; Ontario 7.2.5; OSHA 1910.146) were not re-read on
    their pages by this review (the third 1.24.30 review read them).
  - npm test was not run; only tests/station.js (46 pass) and this replay.
